summary: Moses prayer: Lord you have been our dwelling place in all generations before mountains brought forth or ever you formed earth and world even from everlasting to everlasting you are God. You turn man to destruction and say return children of men for thousand years in your sight like yesterday when past and as watch in night, you carry them away as with flood they are as sleep in morning like grass which grows in morning flourishes in evening cut down withers. For we are consumed by anger and troubled, you have set our iniquities before you secret sins in light of your face, for all our days pass away in your wrath we bring years to end as sigh. Days of our years are 70 or by reason of strength 80 yet is their pride labor and sorrow for it is soon cut off and we fly away. Who knows power of anger and your wrath according to fear that is due? So teach us to number our days that we may get heart of wisdom. Return Yahweh how long? Have compassion on servants, satisfy us early with lovingkindness that we may rejoice and be glad all days, make us glad according to days you have afflicted and years we have seen evil, let your work appear to servants and your glory to children, let favor of Lord our God be upon us and establish work of hands of us upon us.
whyItMatters: Only Psalm of Moses, contrasts everlasting God with fleeting humanity, teaches to number days for wisdom, and asks for favor to establish work of hands.

keyVerses.text: A Prayer by Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations.
keyVerses.why: Dwelling place — maon — home, not just existence but habitation.

keyVerses.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
keyVerses.why: Number days to get heart of wisdom — awareness of finitude leads to wisdom.

keyVerses.text: Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
keyVerses.why: Favor establish work of hands — prayer for permanence in fleeting life.

questions.question: What does 'Lord you have been our dwelling place in all generations' mean with everlasting to everlasting?
questions.answer: Moses says Lord you have been maon dwelling place, home, refuge in all generations — before mountains born or earth and world formed from everlasting to everlasting you are God. Contrasts God's eternity with human transience. Everlasting to everlasting (meolam ad olam) — from hidden time to hidden time. Dwelling place not building but God himself as home — Israel had no land yet, God is home. For modern transience, God as dwelling place across generations.

questions.question: Why 'thousand years like yesterday' and '70 or 80 years labor sorrow'? Is life short?
questions.answer: You turn man to destruction and say return children of men — dust to dust. Thousand years in sight like yesterday when past and as watch in night (3-4 hour night shift). Human time vs divine time. Then you carry them away as flood, as sleep, morning like grass flourishes evening cut withers — grass that grows morning cut down evening. Days 70 or by strength 80 yet pride labor sorrow soon cut off fly away — realistic lifespan in ancient and modern still ~70-80 average. Brings years to end as sigh (hegeh — whisper). Who knows power of anger? Therefore teach us to number days that we may get heart of wisdom — awareness of finitude leads to wisdom, not despair.

questions.question: What does 'satisfy us early with lovingkindness make glad according days afflicted favor establish work of hands' mean?
questions.answer: Return Yahweh how long? Have compassion, satisfy us early (boker — morning) with lovingkindness (hesed) that we may rejoice and be glad all days. Make glad according days you have afflicted and years seen evil — measure for measure joy for sorrow proportion. Let work appear to servants and glory to children — let your work be visible. Let favor of Lord be upon us and establish work of hands — repeated — in fleeting life, ask for permanence: may what we do with hands last, be established by God's favor, not just vanish like grass. Prayer for joy and lasting impact despite brevity.

glossary.def: Home, refuge, habitation — God himself as home across generations.
Awareness of finitude leading to heart of wisdom, not morbidity.
Make permanent, give lasting meaning to fleeting labor.
